title: Original recipe directions and design knowledge
description: All existing independently authored Dial In directions, with source links, photographic intent, tradeoffs, adaptation guidance and limits. Seven camera slots are a per-shoot output limit, not a library limit. These unrendered starting points are not copied creator recipes or measured photographic-quality results.

recipes.title: Faithful everyday color
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Start with REALA ACE's varied-subject color and avoid a strong global cast.

recipe.name: Everyday color
recipe.why: A restrained color baseline for varied subjects.

design.rationale: Start with REALA ACE's varied-subject color and avoid a strong global cast.
design.tradeoff: Its firmer highlights can still be harsh on a bright face; DR200 is not clipping insurance.
design.adaptation: Decide DR and tones from highlight priority; preserve a requested cast instead of automatic neutrality.
limitations: Uncalibrated JPEG color is not exact product-color proof.
Auto WB adapts; it cannot guarantee skin across different light sources.

recipes.title: Gentle people
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Use Pro Neg Std's soft portrait gradation, then judge whether additional softening is necessary.

recipe.name: Gentle faces
recipe.why: Gentler gradation for people when strong contrast is unwanted.

design.rationale: Use Pro Neg Std's soft portrait gradation, then judge whether additional softening is necessary.
design.tradeoff: Can lose useful separation in flat light; it does not smooth away skin texture.
design.adaptation: Consider stronger tone separation for flat light, rather than declaring this the universal skin recipe.

sources.title: Fujifilm PRO Neg. Std and Hi characteristics
Fujifilm simulation use and filter behavior

limitations: Pro Neg Hi is a distinct base, not an exact equivalent produced by slider changes.
Actual skin and lighting still need review.

recipes.title: Quiet documentary
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Classic Chrome's restraint supports a quiet record without treating every photograph as nostalgia.

recipe.name: Quiet story
recipe.why: Restrained color lets gesture and surroundings lead.

design.rationale: Classic Chrome's restraint supports a quiet record without treating every photograph as nostalgia.
design.tradeoff: Muted reds and stronger shadows may cost important clothing color or face detail.
design.adaptation: Protect a face with exposure and gentler tones; choose a different base when the red hue is the subject.
limitations: Not an exact historical film-stock reproduction.
A documentary style is interpretation, not colorimetric neutrality.

recipes.title: Warm memory
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: A family-memory intention can justify warmth and texture; the numeric recipe here is independently authored.

recipe.name: Warm memory
recipe.why: A deliberate warm album interpretation, with restrained texture.

design.rationale: A family-memory intention can justify warmth and texture; the numeric recipe here is independently authored.
design.tradeoff: Amber highlights plus warm WB shifts can push skin orange; warm ambient lamps increase that risk.
design.adaptation: Reduce the added cast before replacing the base if faces are too orange. Keep warmth only when requested.

sources.title: Nathalie Boucry: family-memory intention and light-dependent tradeoffs
Josh Edgoose with Fujifilm: intention and recipe design

limitations: Inspired by creative intention/tradeoffs, not Boucry's or Edgoose's published numeric recipe.
No diffusion-filter softness or halation is implied.

recipes.title: Deliberate vivid nature
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Velvia already supplies strong color; keep extra color density modest until the scene warrants more.

recipe.name: Vivid nature
recipe.why: Color drama for foliage, flowers and scenic frames.

design.rationale: Velvia already supplies strong color; keep extra color density modest until the scene warrants more.
design.tradeoff: Already saturated subjects and skin may become dense; FX Blue can over-darken an important blue surface.
design.adaptation: Choose blue depth separately from red/green detail; fixed Daylight may need changing under new illumination.

sources.title: Fujifilm simulation use and filter behavior

limitations: Not automatically appropriate because it is sunny.
Does not guarantee saturated-channel or highlight recovery.

recipes.title: Saturated color detail
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Separate saturated-color gradation from the overall Color slider and preserve the important hue.

recipe.name: Color detail
recipe.why: Explore gradation in saturated objects without extra overall color.

design.rationale: Separate saturated-color gradation from the overall Color slider and preserve the important hue.
design.tradeoff: Stronger Chrome can change density beyond the desired object; compare with it Off.
design.adaptation: Use the mildest strength that serves visible detail; do not claim it removes glare or fixes sensor clipping.
limitations: A processing effect cannot replace lighting or optical reflection control.
Precise product color needs a controlled color workflow beyond this proposal.

recipes.title: Faces in mixed interiors
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Begin with adaptable Auto WB; diagnose the dominant subject light before adding a green/magenta correction.

recipe.name: Mixed interior
recipe.why: An adaptable starting point for faces and retained room atmosphere.

design.rationale: Begin with adaptable Auto WB; diagnose the dominant subject light before adding a green/magenta correction.
design.tradeoff: One WB cannot neutralize differently lit regions; keeping ambience may leave some cast.
design.adaptation: DR100 here is provisional for modest contrast, not an indoor rule. Bright windows/signs may justify higher DR.

sources.title: Fujifilm PRO Neg. Std and Hi characteristics

limitations: No precise Kelvin is inferred from a phone JPEG.
Auto WB and zero shift do not guarantee neutrality under LED spectra.

recipes.title: Gentle monochrome separation
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Yellow filtering provides milder blue separation than red, on ACROS's own tonal/texture base.

recipe.name: Gentle B&W
recipe.why: A quieter monochrome interpretation of gesture and form.

design.rationale: Yellow filtering provides milder blue separation than red, on ACROS's own tonal/texture base.
design.tradeoff: Loses meaningful hue information; native monochrome tint is not represented by this Recipe.
design.adaptation: Use only where color is optional, and check the camera's tint when neutral B&W matters.

sources.title: Fujifilm simulation use and filter behavior

limitations: The signature is not a neutral-tint guarantee.
Added grain is distinct from ACROS's embedded ISO-dependent texture.

recipes.title: Dramatic monochrome separation
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: Red filtering darkens blues relative to reds, useful only when those relationships serve the photograph.

recipe.name: Graphic B&W
recipe.why: Stronger color-to-tone separation for a deliberate graphic interpretation.

design.rationale: Red filtering darkens blues relative to reds, useful only when those relationships serve the photograph.
design.tradeoff: Harder shadows can lose face detail; a red object becomes lighter relative to a blue one.
design.adaptation: Retain intentional silhouette rather than automatically lifting every face; choose gentler filtering for another goal.

sources.title: Fujifilm simulation use and filter behavior

limitations: Not mandatory for midday, indoors or any particular weather.
Native monochrome tint remains unknown.

recipes.title: Gentle skin with surrounding color
recipes.author: Dial In
recipes.description: ASTIA can treat skin gently while retaining vivid surrounding blues/greens; it is not uniformly muted.

recipe.name: Skin and color
recipe.why: An unmapped native alternative for skin and lively surroundings.

design.rationale: ASTIA can treat skin gently while retaining vivid surrounding blues/greens; it is not uniformly muted.
design.tradeoff: Native X100VI support does not establish a permitted new settings-file write in the current map.
design.adaptation: An already-kept ASTIA bank can remain exact; a new mapped substitute must be called a compromise.

sources.title: Fujifilm simulation use and filter behavior

limitations: Reference-only for new writes until mapping/acceptance evidence exists.
Pro Neg Std does not become an identical ASTIA rendering by copying these sliders.
